brief: Rain falls on a town whose ground has no memory of it. wetF()/stepWet is ONE global scalar that seats, moss and the light read; grep returns no per-cell water term anywhere in the source. So a shower wets everything by the same amount and dries it by the same amount, and the half-hour after rain looks like the half-hour before. Give the paved ground PUDDLES: per-cell variance (hash(x, y+k) > c) at the grain the lane is addressed by, filling while raining, standing where the feet already wear the ground (trod[]/wear[]), drying back with wetF over its ~3 h, dark enough to read from the wide shot and holding the LANE_LAMPS after dusk. Scope it to the lane and the cross street; the plaza's paving belongs to the two moss regions and can come later.
successLooksLike: The hour after a shower is visibly different from the hour before it at the wide shot — the lane holds water in the worn places and loses it slowly — and after dusk the lamps have something to sit in.
avoid: Do not make it global: a uniform wet sheen is what wetF already does and it reads as nothing. Do not extend the moss CA — this is water, it is fast, and it belongs to the rain, not to the year. A puddle that changes on a minute's scale is a LIVE overlay, not a ground-cache repaint; and a reflection drawn before applyLight's multiply is slate by midnight.
